premises.text: Once a game integrates Web3, its in-game economy becomes a real economy that can crash and must be managed like a macroeconomic system
premises.evidence_span: as soon as you build a web 3 game Your game economy becomes a real economy

premises.text: Prior Web3 game strategies of marketing spend and one-dimensional staking are insufficient to keep economies healthy
premises.evidence_span: spend it on marketing to new players to bring new players into the ecosystem

premises.text: Healthy economies require participants to produce in-economy and tax-like sinks that create currency value
premises.evidence_span: the people who are participating in the economy should be able to produce in that economy

premises.text: Platform features such as on-chain minigames, crafting, activity rewards, leaderboards, and security bots implement those principles
premises.evidence_span: we have on-chain minigames, on-chain crafting, Minecraft style

premises.text: Pricing combines a $1,000/month economy-monitoring fee with $0.10 per user interaction as infrastructure
premises.evidence_span: we charge $1,000 per month to anyone who wants to know what's going on in an on-chain economy

value.text: Economic infrastructure that helps Web3 games keep healthy, engaging player economies
value.evidence_span: We build economic infrastructure for Web3 games
